rows.selection_reason: With no prior experiments, the key uncertainty is whether multimodal fusion (RNA + image) with multiprofile aggregation provides a meaningful accuracy boost over unimodal baselines, and which component choices matter most. Config_002 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, concat) serves as a strong, moderate-cost baseline: it tests the core multimodal hypothesis with a learned RNA encoder (scvi_n200), a standard image encoder (resnet50), a simple aggregation (avgpool), and the simplest fusion (concat). This is not the most expensive configuration (no transformer aggregation, no ViT-L), so it preserves GPU budget for follow-up experiments that can isolate which axis (RNA encoder, image encoder, aggregation, fusion) drives performance. The result will anchor the search: if accuracy is strong, we exploit by upgrading individual components (e.g., transformer aggregation or ViT-L); if weak, we pivot to unimodal baselines or simpler encoders. Expected relative cost: moderate—multiprofile processing and a learned RNA encoder add cost, but avgpool and resnet50 keep it well below the most expensive configs (ViT-L + transformer).

With only one completed experiment (config_002, acc=0.6315, 7.27 GPU-hrs), evidence is sparse and the most important uncertainty is whether the simple avgpool aggregation in the multiprofile setting is suboptimal. Config_018 is a clean single-variable change from config_002: it replaces avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping all other settings identical (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, concat fusion). Transformer aggregation allows the model to learn profile-level attention weights, which is a well-motivated improvement when multiple profiles carry heterogeneous signal. This experiment directly tests whether a more expressive aggregation mechanism can lift accuracy beyond 0.63. Expected relative cost: moderately higher than config_002 (~8–10 GPU-hrs, roughly 10–40% more) due to the added self-attention layers in the transformer, but still well within budget given 8 experiments remain. This is the best use of experiment 2 because it isolates one high-impact architectural choice without confounding variables, giving clear signal for subsequent decisions.

Evidence: Transformer aggregation clearly outperforms avgpool (+5.6% accuracy: 0.6878 vs 0.6315) with the same scvi_n200/resnet50/concat setup, making transformer the proven aggregation choice. The largest unexplored architectural variable is the image encoder: resnet50 is a relatively modest CNN, while imagenet_vit_l (ViT-Large) offers substantially richer visual representations. This experiment (config_028) isolates the image-encoder upgrade by keeping all other settings identical to the current best (config_018: scvi_n200, transformer, concat, multiprofile), so any accuracy change can be attributed to the image encoder. Rationale: With 7 experiments remaining, testing the highest-impact unexplored dimension (image representation quality) is more informative than a small fusion-method tweak (concat→weighted). If ViT-L delivers a meaningful gain, subsequent experiments can layer in weighted fusion or scgpt on top. Expected cost: ViT-L is considerably larger than ResNet50, so I estimate ~9–12 GPU hours (roughly 2× the 5.16 h of config_018), but the potential accuracy uplift justifies the higher compute spend relative to a marginal fusion change.

Evidence: The three completed experiments show a clear progression: transformer aggregation beats avgpool (+5.6 pp), and imagenet_vit_l beats resnet50 (+3.3 pp), with config_028 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, concat, multiprofile) achieving the best accuracy at 0.7207. The only untested variable in this top configuration is the fusion strategy (concat vs. weighted). Question: Does weighted fusion improve over concat when the strong transformer+ViT-L backbone is already in place? This is a single-variable exploitation of the best-performing setup, directly testing whether the fusion mechanism can squeeze additional accuracy from the same representations. Why this is the best next experiment: With 6 experiments remaining, exploiting the strongest direction first locks in a high-accuracy baseline early. Config_039 differs from config_028 only in fusion (weighted vs. concat), so any accuracy change is cleanly attributable to fusion. Expected cost is similar to config_028 (~4.6–5.0 GPU hours) since the architecture is nearly identical—only the final fusion layer changes—making it a cheap, high-information experiment.

The current best (config_039, acc=0.7250) uses scvi_n200 as the RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion. The only major unexplored dimension in this proven architecture is the RNA encoder. Config_036 swaps scvi_n200 for scgpt while keeping all other settings at their best-known values (imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted, multiprofile). This directly tests whether a different learned RNA encoder can push accuracy beyond 0.7250 or confirm that scvi_n200 is near-optimal. If scgpt performs comparably, we gain confidence the RNA encoder is not the bottleneck; if it improves, we identify a new best. Expected cost is moderate (~4–5 GPU hours), similar to config_039's 3.60 h since the dominant cost drivers (ViT-L image encoder + transformer aggregation) are unchanged, with scgpt adding a modest overhead over scvi_n200. With 5 experiments remaining, this is the highest-information experiment that exploits the strongest evidence while exploring the largest untested design axis.

The current best is config_039 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) at 0.7250 acc. The evidence strongly favors imagenet_vit_l over resnet50, transformer over avgpool, and weighted over concat, while scvi_n200 dominates scgpt (0.725 vs 0.52). The one major untested variable within this best-performing family is the RNA encoder pca_n2000. Config_041 (pca_n2000, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) directly tests whether the simpler, cheaper PCA encoder can match scvi_n200 in the top configuration. If it performs comparably, we confirm a cheaper alternative; if it underperforms, we lock in scvi_n200 as the definitive RNA encoder and can spend remaining budget on finer refinements. This is the highest-information experiment available: it resolves the last major design-axis uncertainty in the promising region without venturing into low-probability areas (e.g., scgpt, which already showed a 20-point accuracy drop). Expected cost: pca_n2000 is a linear projection (no learned encoder), so training should be slightly cheaper than config_039's 3.60 GPU hours—estimated ~3.0–3.5 GPU hours, keeping total budget well within limits.

Evidence: config_039 (scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, transformer, weighted) is the current best at 0.7250 accuracy. All four design dimensions point to this combination: scvi_n200 >> pca/scgpt for RNA, imagenet_vit_l > resnet50 for image, transformer > avgpool for aggregation, and weighted ≥ concat for fusion. The remaining uncertainty is whether the transformer aggregation advantage (seen with resnet50: 0.688 vs 0.632) is robust when paired with the stronger imagenet_vit_l encoder, or whether avgpool + weighted fusion could be nearly as good at lower cost. This experiment (config_021: scvi_n200, imagenet_vit_l, avgpool, weighted) is the single closest untested variant to our best config, changing only the aggregation. If it lands within ~0.01 of 0.7250, it offers a cheaper alternative; if it drops substantially, it confirms transformer is essential and we can confidently lock in config_039 as the final answer with the remaining 2 experiments. Expected cost: slightly lower than config_039's 3.60 GPU hours since avgpool is computationally simpler than a transformer aggregator, likely ~3.0–3.5 GPU hours.

The current best (config_039, 0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted in the multiprofile setting. All 7 completed experiments are multiprofile, so the singleprofile dimension is completely unexplored. config_007 tests whether a single profile (no aggregation step) with the best-known encoders (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l) and weighted fusion can match or exceed the multiprofile result. This is critical because: (1) it reduces model complexity and training cost (no transformer aggregation), (2) it clarifies whether the multiprofile aggregation is genuinely adding signal or just adding parameters, and (3) if it matches the current best at lower cost, it frees GPU budget for the final 2 experiments to explore other directions. Expected cost: ~2.5–3.0 GPU hours (cheaper than config_039's 3.60 since there is no multiprofile transformer aggregation). This is the highest-information experiment remaining: it either confirms multiprofile is necessary or reveals a simpler, cheaper path to comparable accuracy.

The current best (config_039, acc=0.725) uses scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + transformer + weighted + multiprofile. All individual factor comparisons strongly support this combination: scvi_n200 >> scgpt/pca, imagenet_vit_l > resnet50, transformer > avgpool, weighted > concat, multiprofile >> singleprofile. Config_004 is the only remaining untested multiprofile configuration with the best RNA and image encoders (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l), using avgpool + concat. Testing it confirms that the transformer+weighted pairing is indeed superior and rules out any unexpected interaction that could push accuracy above 0.725. Based on config_021 (avgpool+weighted, 0.706) and config_028 (transformer+concat, 0.721), config_004 is expected to land around 0.68–0.70, well below the current best. Its expected cost is moderate (~4–5 GPU hours, comparable to config_021's 4.82 h since it uses avgpool rather than transformer). This is the best use of experiment 9 because it closes the last meaningful gap in the multiprofile scvi_n200+ViT-L design space, leaving experiment 10 free for a minimal-cost run to keep total GPU hours low.

Evidence: All four aggregation×fusion combinations for the clearly superior base (scvi_n200 + imagenet_vit_l + multiprofile) have been tested, with config_039 (transformer+weighted) at 0.725 being the best. RNA encoder (scvi_n200 >> scgpt/pca), image encoder (vit_l >> resnet50), and profile setting (multiprofile >> singleprofile) are all well-established. No remaining untested configuration falls in the promising region; all alternatives involve a materially weaker component. Question: Since no untested config can plausibly exceed 0.725, this final experiment should minimize additional GPU cost. config_032 (rna_only, singleprofile, pca_n2000) is the simplest possible architecture—no image processing, no aggregation, no fusion—so its expected training cost is very low (~0.2–0.5 GPU hours), the cheapest option in the untested pool. Rationale: The best validation accuracy (0.725) is already secured; running the cheapest remaining config minimizes total GPU hours (currently 37.93) while satisfying the budget constraint, making this the most cost-efficient use of the final experiment slot.
